name: Non-syndromic Uterovaginal Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Classification for Müllerian Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of congenital uterine and/or vaginal structural anomalies without associated syndromic features
No evidence of renal, skeletal, or other systemic malformations
Confirmation of uterovaginal malformation by pelvic MRI or 3D ultrasound
Symptoms such as primary amenorrhea or dyspareunia consistent with uterovaginal malformation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital uterovaginal structural anomaly confirmed by imaging with absence of extrareproductive anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis excludes syndromic forms with associated systemic malformations

searchTerms: born without uterus or small uterus

pathognomonic.symptomName: Vaginal agenesis or transverse vaginal septum

searchTerms: difficulty getting pregnant from uterus issue
unable to conceive due to uterus problem

common.symptomName: Pelvic pain associated with obstructive anomalies

occasional.symptomName: Urinary tract infections secondary to anatomical distortion
searchTerms: UTIs caused by urinary tract distortion
repeated bladder infections due to structure issues
menstrual cycle problems including scanty flow

occasional.symptomName: Psychological distress related to reproductive dysfunction
searchTerms: psychological issues due to fertility problems
mental health affected by reproductive dysfunction

rare.symptomName: Endometriosis secondary to obstructive uterovaginal anomaly
searchTerms: uterine lining growth due to obstruction

rare.symptomName: Secondary hematocolpos due to vaginal obstruction
searchTerms: blood buildup in vagina due to blockage
vaginal blood collection secondary to blockage

laboratory: Normal hormonal profile (FSH, LH, estrogen) in most cases
imaging: Pelvic MRI showing uterine and vaginal structural anomalies
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence typical
other: Normal renal ultrasound to exclude associated anomalies
Physical examination revealing absent or shortened vaginal canal

distinguishingFeatures: Syndromic uterovaginal agenesis with associated renal and skeletal anomalies
Often includes hearing loss or other systemic features
Absent uterus and upper vagina with testes present

redFlags: Presence of renal or skeletal malformations suggesting syndromic condition
Severe pelvic pain indicating obstructive complications
Primary amenorrhea with absent uterus on imaging
references: American Society for Reproductive Medicine. The ASRM classification of Müllerian anomalies. Fertil Steril. 2021.
Rock JA, Zacur HA. Müllerian anomalies and their management. Obstet Gynecol Clin North Am. 2017.
